subject: Animation
title: Research Trips: Living the Story
description: A short lesson to help you apply Research Trips: Living the Story.

hook.text: Before making a Pixar film, the team goes on research trips to live inside the story's world.

buildup.text: For Up, artists traveled to Venezuela's tepui mountains. For Coco, they visited Mexican villages.

discovery.text: The trips give animators details no reference photo can provide — smells, sounds, and feelings.

twist.text: For Finding Nemo, the entire team got scuba certified. For Ratatouille, they ate at fine Paris restaurants.

climax.text: These research trips are expensive, but Pixar considers them essential for authentic storytelling.

punchline.text: Pixar animates what it has touched, tasted, and breathed.

quiz.question: Why does Pixar send teams on research trips?
options: To experience the story's world firsthand and capture authentic sensory details
To scout filming locations for live-action versions

details.summary: Pixar sends filmmakers on extensive research trips to live the experiences they animate. The Finding Nemo team scuba-dived. The Up team explored Venezuelan tepuis. The Coco team spent years in Mexico. This firsthand research fills films with authentic details audiences unconsciously recognize.
details.whyItMatters: Research trips explain why Pixar worlds feel lived-in rather than imagined. Firsthand experience provides the countless small authentic details that the audience cannot consciously identify but unconsciously values as truth.
takeaways: Pixar sends production teams on extensive research trips for each film
Firsthand experience fills films with authentic details audiences sense
The Finding Nemo team scuba-dived; the Up team explored Venezuelan tepuis

faq.question: What research trips has Pixar taken for specific films?
faq.answer: The Finding Nemo team studied marine biology and scuba diving. Ratatouille researchers ate at Paris's finest restaurants and toured kitchens. The Coco team spent years in Mexican communities. The Soul team consulted jazz musicians, metaphysicians, and therapists.

faq.question: Why can't filmmakers just research online?
faq.answer: Internet research provides facts; physical experience provides feeling. The way light moves underwater, how a professional kitchen sounds during service, what a Venezuelan tepui smells like — these sensory details inform artistic decisions that online research cannot provide.
